brief:
King's College London has lifted the suspension of student activist Usama Ghanem following his disciplinary case related to pro-Palestine activism, according to Middle East Eye. The university had suspended Ghanem over his campus organizing work supporting Palestinian causes.

The reversal comes after a year-long process during which the student's case remained under review. The exact grounds for the initial suspension and any conditions attached to his reinstatement were not disclosed by the institution. Ghanem's case drew attention as universities across Britain faced mounting scrutiny over their handling of student activism and campus speech related to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
